tools.name: read_docx
tools.description:
Reads a DOCX file. Returns text with inline CriticMarkup for Tracked Changes and Comments: {++inserted++}, {--deleted--}, {==highlighted==}{>>comment<<}. Set clean_view=True for the finalized 'Accepted' text without markup.

Modes:
- 'full' (default): paginated body content. Use page=N to navigate.
- 'outline': heading map only — start here for large docs to plan targeted reads. Defaults to L1-L2 headings; pass outline_max_level=3-6 to see deeper structure.
- 'appendix': defined terms, anchors, and cross-reference targets. Consult before editing legal/technical docs to avoid breaking references.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the DOCX file.

clean_view.description: If False (default), returns the 'Raw' text with inline CriticMarkup. If True, returns 'Accepted' text.

mode.description: 'full' returns body content. 'outline' returns a structural heading map. 'appendix' returns defined terms.

page.description: Page number (1-indexed) for mode='full'. Defaults to 1.

outline_max_level.description: For mode='outline' only: cap on heading depth.

tools.name: process_document_batch
tools.description:
Applies a batch of edits and review actions to a DOCX.

All changes evaluate against the ORIGINAL document state — do not chain dependent edits within one batch (e.g. rename X to Y, then modify Y). Apply the rename first, then send a second batch.

Each item in `changes` must specify a `type`:
1. 'modify': Search-and-replace. `target_text` must uniquely match — include surrounding context if the phrase is ambiguous. `new_text` supports Markdown: '# Heading 1' through '###### Heading 6', '**bold**', '_italic_', and '\n\n' to split into multiple paragraphs. Empty `new_text` deletes. Do NOT write CriticMarkup tags ({++, {--, {>>) manually — use the `comment` parameter for comments.
2. 'accept' / 'reject': Finalize or revert a tracked change by `target_id` (e.g. 'Chg:12').
3. 'reply': Reply to a comment by `target_id` (e.g. 'Com:5') with `text`.
4. 'insert_row' / 'delete_row': Table edits. Disk mode only — not supported on Live Word canvas.

ID VOLATILITY: 'Chg:N' and 'Com:N' shift between document states. Always call `read_docx` immediately before any accept/reject/reply — do not reuse IDs from earlier in the conversation.

`author_name` is used for attribution on all tracked changes and comments, in both disk and Live Word modes.

original_docx_path.description: Absolute path to the source file.

author_name.description: Name to appear in Track Changes (e.g., 'Reviewer AI').

changes.description: List of changes to apply. Each change must specify 'type'.

tools.name: accept_all_changes
tools.description: Accepts all tracked changes and removes all comments in a single operation, producing a finalized clean document. Use this when a document review is entirely complete and you want to clear all redlines.

docx_path.description: Absolute path to the DOCX file.

tools.name: diff_docx_files
tools.description: Compares two DOCX files and returns a unified diff of their text content. Useful for analyzing differences between versions before editing.

original_path.description: Absolute path to the baseline DOCX file.

modified_path.description: Absolute path to the modified DOCX file.

compare_clean.description: If True, compares 'Accepted' state. If False, compares raw text.

tools.name: finalize_document
tools.description: Prepares a document for external distribution or e-signature. This tool combines metadata sanitization, document locking (protection), and markup resolution into a single step. NOTE: PDF export and AES encryption are disabled in this environment.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the DOCX file.

sanitize_mode.description: full removes all markup, keep-markup redacts metadata but keeps comments/redlines.

accept_all.description: If true, auto-accepts all unresolved track changes before finalizing.

protection_mode.description: Native OOXML document locking. encrypt falls back to read_only in this environment.

author.description: Replace all remaining markup authorship with this name.

tools.name: login_to_adeu_cloud
tools.description: Logs the user into the Adeu Cloud backend. Securely opens a browser window for authentication.

tools.name: logout_of_adeu_cloud
tools.description: Logs out of the Adeu Cloud backend by clearing the local API key.

tools.name: search_and_fetch_emails
tools.description: Searches the user's live email inbox. By default, searches only the Inbox folder. Returns a list of lightweight previews. Call again with `email_id` to fetch the full body and download attachments.

tools.name: create_email_draft
tools.description: Creates an email draft in the user's native draft box. Provide `reply_to_email_id` to reply, or `subject` and `to_recipients` for a new email.

explanations.title: Path traversal
explanations.why_it_matters: Traversal sequences can escape an intended directory boundary and reach unrelated files.
explanations.remediation: Canonicalize paths, verify the resolved path remains under an allowlisted root, and reject traversal forms.

explanations.title: Sensitive file access
explanations.why_it_matters: Broad file access can expose credentials, private configuration, or user data to a tool caller.
explanations.remediation: Restrict access to an explicit root and allowlisted files, and enforce permissions independently of caller input.

explanations.title: Unrestricted network access
explanations.why_it_matters: Unrestricted outbound connectivity can enable data disclosure or access to unintended services.
explanations.remediation: Restrict egress to required destinations and protocols, and validate destinations before connecting.

explanations.title: Context stuffing with long descriptions
explanations.why_it_matters: Excessive tool metadata can crowd out relevant context and make malicious or important content harder to review.
explanations.remediation: Keep descriptions concise, enforce reasonable size limits, and review unusually large metadata.

explanations.title: Data disclosure through remote fetch
explanations.why_it_matters: A tool that combines sensitive data with an uncontrolled network request can disclose information to third parties.
explanations.remediation: Do not send secrets to caller-controlled destinations, minimize transmitted data, and enforce destination allowlists.
